sections.body: Ansor broadens tensor-program search with a two-level sketch-and-annotation representation, complete-program sampling, evolutionary fine-tuning, and a learned cost model, allowing it to find programs outside existing search-framework spaces.
sections.heading: Ansor's search representation

sections.body: Other compiler systems likewise depend on representation choices: super-blocks convert hot traces into linear optimization regions, machine-learning compilers rely on quantifiable program features, and WCC raises assembly-level WCET facts back to source-level structures for optimization.
sections.heading: Representation choices in other compilers

sections.body: The shared concept is that better intermediate representations do not merely store program facts; they determine which transformations, predictions, and search paths become practical.
sections.heading: Synthesis angle

title: Representations Expand the Compiler Search Space
